text:
Sam R.: FYI, noticed a spike in provisioning failures in us-west-3 after last night's BIOS microcode push. Lots of nodes stuck in 'provisioning' with PXE timeouts.
Lia M.: confirmed, I saw ~42 nodes stuck across two racks. BMC logs show repeated keepalive disconnects right after the BIOS update.
Raj P.: can you paste the BMC error snippet? might be a watchdog interaction with new microcode.
Lia M.: logs from node-gw-12: `IPMI SYSINFO: BMC keepalive lost, reinit network, reboot planned` then `tftp: timeout waiting for block 1` repeatedly.
ops-oncall: deploy-bot triggered an alert at 03:12 UTC for provisioning-backlog.usw3, paging oncall.
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2247. Affected capacity: 68 GPUs flagged as "unavailable" for scheduling.
Sam R.: looks like the BIOS microcode changed the NIC boot ordering on some BMC firmware combos; OOB still up intermittently but not long enough for PXE to complete.
Raj P.: Is this limited to a specific BMC firmware? I saw similar patterns when BMC fw 2.14.x met BIOS 1.3.7 on older boards.
Lia M.: yes, cross referencing inventory: nodes show BMC 2.14.0 and BIOS 1.3.7 on the failing hosts. Canary nodes with BMC 2.15 or BIOS 1.3.6 are fine.
infra-sre: recommend immediate throttling of the rollout and a canary rollback to previous BIOS on the remaining batch. Also suggest pinning PXE server retries + increasing TFTP window as short-term mitigation.
Sam R.: Agreed. Lia, can you run blocklist for nodes in rack 12 and 13 in us-west-3? Command: `inventory block add --reason "bios-microcode-pause" --nodes rack12:* rack13:*`
Lia M.: running now. Also increasing tftp timeout to 15s on the PXE hosts: `echo 15 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tftp_timeout` (will make a deploy to all pxes).
ops-oncall: note: provisioning backlog causing scheduler to spin up extra reserved benches in eu-west to absorb jobs. That added ~$9k in excess spot/overflow costs overnight. Finance pinged.
Raj P.: Ouch. Need a cost mitigation note in the incident: fallback to draining queued workloads to dedicated pools before spinning ephemeral capacity.
Sam R.: Action items: 1) pause BIOS rollout (I filed rollout-pause), 2) roll back BIOS on failing nodes via netboot image-rollback, 3) schedule BMC fw audit, 4) postmortem template.
Lia M.: rolling back 8 nodes now, progress: 3/8 completed, one node hit `u-boot: secureboot flag toggled` during rollback — paused and moved to manual queue.
infra-sre: if secureboot toggles are happening, we need to check NVRAM write path. That could explain the intermittent boot ordering. Add owners: firmware (Sam), oob (Raj).
Sam R.: tagging @firmware-team and @oob-team. Lia, keep the manual queue list updated in INC-2026-2247.
Lia M.: done. Adding snippets to the incident thread.
ops-oncall: please add a note for customers: capacity degradation in us-west-3 for GPU reserved pools until remediation completes. I'll draft a brief status.
Raj P.: one more data point: BMCs that were dual-staged (outdated BMC + recent BIOS) rebooted into a BMC-recovery loop after PXE fail; we should exclude them from automatic reboots.
Sam R.: temporary change: disable auto-reboot on provision-failures for the next 6 hours: `provisioner config set auto_reboot_on_fail false --scope us-west-3`
Lia M.: done. That prevented 12 immediate reboot loops.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused: bios-upgrade-v1.3.7 -> status PAUSED by Sam R.
infra-sre: next steps: run full fleet scan for BMC 2.14.x + BIOS 1.3.7 intersections, prepare targeted rollback plan, and validate PXE/TFTP retry behavior in a sandbox.
Sam R.: I'll own the rollback schedule and coordinate with firmware team. Raj, lia — please prepare a short runbook for manual repro and a checklist for next canary (including tftp timeout, disable auto-reboot, and BMC fw requirement).
Lia M.: will add repro steps and `ipmitool` snippets to the runbook. Example: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U admin sdr elist` + `ipmitool fru print 0` to confirm board version.
ops-oncall: timeline update: rollback in progress, estimated 3 hours to clear provisioning backlog. Posting to status page now.
Sam R.: thanks all. We'll reconvene in 90m or on shorter notice if situation degrades. :thumbsup:
